after.focus: Finish cooked turkey with herbs and keep lettuce dry
after.outcome: Crumbled cooked turkey with softened peppers, fresh mint/cilantro and intact lettuce cups.
before: Wash and dry lettuce and herbs before handling the raw turkey. Keep the ready-to-eat leaves separate from the raw meat and its utensils.

The original route uses a 12-inch skillet for one pound turkey and two peppers. A scaled batch needs enough pan space; use separate loads or vessels and divide all measured oil and seasonings proportionally.

checkpoints.cue: The crumbled turkey reaches 165°F / 74°C before herbs enter.
checkpoints.why: The five-minute estimate and loss of pink do not establish ground-poultry doneness.

checkpoints.cue: Filling is moist without a large puddle when spooned into the dry leaves.
checkpoints.why: Pooled liquid quickly softens the leaves.

troubleshooting.cause: Wet leaves or pooled pan liquid are combined too early.
troubleshooting.fix: Dry the leaves, allow excess cooking liquid to reduce as directed after the turkey is cooked, and assemble just before eating. Keep the full oil and fish-sauce amounts.

substitutions.alternative: For a sweeter original-size four-portion batch, stir 1/2 tsp sugar into the cooked filling with the herbs and lime; scale that alternative amount with the full batch.
substitutions.effect: This separate sweet finish changes the filling. The main method keeps sugar out and offers hoisin at the table; do not add a second unmeasured sugar dose.

after.timing: Allow about 25 minutes for the current original batch, with 15 minutes preparation and about 10 minutes stovetop work/assembly. The 3-minute pepper stage, 30-second garlic stage and roughly 5-minute turkey stage are initial estimates; the thermometer endpoint and any liquid reduction can take longer. Most stovetop cooking is active, and extra loads extend elapsed time.
after.storage: Store cooked filling separately from dry lettuce and sauces. Refrigerate in shallow containers within 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F / 32°C, at 40°F / 4°C or below. Use filling within 3–4 days and reheat to 165°F / 74°C throughout. Assemble cups after reheating so the leaves stay crisp.

exactBodyChange.before:
## Chef's Note

Fish sauce, lime, cilantro and mint season the turkey filling. Let excess pan liquid reduce before filling the lettuce cups so the leaves stay crisp.

## Directions

1. **Continue:** In 12-inch skillet on medium-high, cook bell peppers in vegetable oil 3 minutes. Add garlic; cook 30 seconds. Add ground turkey and fish sauce. Cook 5 minutes, breaking up meat. Check turkey for 165°F / 74°C before adding the herbs. The unmeasured sugar from the saved method is omitted; offer the listed hoisin on the side.

2. **Continue:** Stir in cilantro, mint leaves, lime juice. Serve in lettuce cups with Sriracha hot sauce, if desired.
exactBodyChange.after:
## Chef's Note

Fish sauce, lime, cilantro and mint season the turkey filling. Let excess pan liquid reduce before filling the lettuce cups so the leaves stay crisp.

## Directions

1. **Cook filling:** In a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat, cook all the bell peppers in all the measured vegetable oil for about 3 minutes. Add all the garlic and cook about 30 seconds, then add all the ground turkey and fish sauce. Break up the meat and start checking after about 5 minutes; continue until the turkey reaches 165°F / 74°C on a thermometer before adding herbs. If liquid pools, let excess liquid reduce while stirring, keeping the filling moist. Use more loads or vessels for a larger batch, dividing the full measured ingredients proportionally.
2. **Finish and serve:** Stir in all the cilantro, mint and lime juice. Spoon the cooked filling into washed, dried lettuce cups using clean utensils. Offer the listed Sriracha and hoisin separately as wanted. Assemble promptly so the leaves stay crisp.
